summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a watchdog agent that executes shell commands from a remote server and exfiltrates host data
details: The package installs a `tt-help watchdog` CLI that polls a remote server (default http://127.0.0.1:3001, with http://117.71.53.99:17301 advertised in shipped scripts and help text as the intended operator endpoint) on a fixed cadence. The heartbeat response's `commands` array is passed unchanged to child_process.spawn (with shell:true on Windows), giving the remote party arbitrary command execution on the host running the watchdog. The same response can push a `clientConfig` that rewrites `~/.tt-help.json`, including the server URL itself, allowing the operator to hand the client over to a different endpoint. Each heartbeat POSTs hostname, external IPv4, OS platform/release/arch, CPU count, memory, node version, uptime, load averages, the full contents of `~/.tt-help.json` (server URL, proxy, browser path, userId, limits), and a tail of child-process stderr logs to `/api/watchdog/heartbeat` and `/api/watchdog/analyze-logs` on the same server. Independently, the watchdog polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and, when a newer version is published, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest`, providing a persistent auto-update channel under the publisher's control. The remote-command sink combined with host/config exfiltration and an auto-pull update path constitutes a backdoor with attacker command-and-control over any host that runs the watchdog.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
